key_insight: The paper shows that Cornucopia ultra-high-rate quantum codes can be turned into a modular architecture that supports universal logical computation with low overhead.
engineering_relevance: This matters because it preserves the memory efficiency of high-rate error correction while adding practical, individually addressable logical operations needed for fault-tolerant quantum computers.
method: Use the [[2844,1426,18]] Cornucopia code as the core block, storing 1,426 logical qubits per module.
Connect blocks with bridges to form a modular quantum computer.
Exploit translation symmetry to build reusable gadgets that address 1,422 logical qubits and support basic, high-throughput, and fixed-extractor instruction sets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that a module capable of running any basic instruction set requires an average of 4.1 physical qubits per logical qubit, versus 3.0 for memory alone.
watch_item: The architecture’s advantage depends on available workspace and excludes magic-state factories, so full system overhead may be higher in practice.
paper_title: A modular quantum computer based on Cornucopia codes
